<b>Set-Figuren werden nicht doppelt gezä: Set figures are not counted twice. A set price at BrickLink is for the complete set, so the minifigures are already in it. Anyone who records sets and their figures separately would otherwise have them twice in the total. So the app counts like this: sets count in full, and of every figure only those copies count that are not sitting in a set of yours.

<b>Was unverändert bleibt.</b> Die <b>St: What stays the same. The quantity does not change – the figures are physically yours, wherever they sit. And paid/profit (Collector-Pro) still uses the full individual value, because there it is about what you actually spent on the items you bought.
<b>Wo bereinigt wird – und wo nicht.</b>: Where it is deducted – and where not. The deduction only applies where sets and figures meet in one number: in the total value, in the collection's value widget with filter All, in the breakdown by type/condition, in the value by release year and in the value curve. If you filter to figures (or sets), you see the full value of that group – there is no second category in play there. Individual cards and the Top 10 always show the item's full individual value too.
<b>Woher die Preise kommen.</b> Für jede: Where the prices come from. For every item the app fetches the average sale prices of the last 6 months from BrickLink – separately for new and used. It always uses the price matching the recorded condition; if that is missing, it falls back to the other one. Items without price data (e.g. manually recorded custom builds) count as 0 € and are listed as "without a price" under the value widget.
